chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi from Musa ibn Umar ibn Bazee' said:

I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, indeed the people have narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would, when he took one path, return by another. So he used to do this.' He said, 'Yes, and I do it often, so you do it.' He said, then he said to me, 'Indeed, it is a provision for you.'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a common phrase of respect)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and practical significance of the Prophet's practice of taking different paths when traveling?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) validates the Sunnah of 'taking a different way' (Ikhlaq) for travelers, linking it directly to increased divine provision (Rizq). This practice, rooted in the Prophet’s (PBUH) habits, is presented not merely as a precautionary measure but as a spiritual mechanism for attracting sustenance, encouraging followers to emulate this prophetic tradition for material and spiritual benefit.
